**Post-Market Brief — Wednesday, 2026-11-04**

_Fire: cron #23 `agentic-post-market-brief`, scheduled 2026-11-04 22:30 ET (US/Eastern)._ _Data as of the 2026-11-04 regular-session close; after-hours tape as of ~22:30 ET._

---

**TL;DR**

- Democrats took both chambers — a "blue tsunami" midterm sweep — and equities ripped: the **Dow +3.03% (+1,569 pts)**, S&P 500 **+1.58%** to 7,688.62, Nasdaq +1.44%, Russell 2000 +1.58%.
- **VIX collapsed 20.3% to 16.61**.
- But the tape was a *rotation*, not a risk-on melt-up: **XLK finished flat, SMH fell 2.75%, and energy -4.74%**, while discretionary +4.26%, financials +3.51% and staples/REITs/communications all added ~3.3–3.5%.
- The pressure point was policy, not earnings —
- CNBC reported the market repriced *limits on AI data centers* after Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa pledged an immediate pause, which crushed the data-center complex (HUT -23.2%, STRL -21.5%, CIFR -20.0%, MOD -21.4%) and dragged semis with it.
- Gold +3.68% and the 10-year yield down to 4.894% say the same thing: lower growth/policy risk, weaker dollar, some flight-to-quality inside an otherwise strong tape.

- **Caveat that changes how to read it:** the rally is one event-driven, one-day re-rating with no volume confirmation in the index ETFs (SPY +1.65% on 61.6M shares vs a 76.9M 30-day average —
- i.e. a *below-average* participation day), and **VIX at 16.61 already prices the shock as resolved** before Thursday's jobless claims and Friday's payrolls.
- Treat the levels as an election gap that still needs a macro test, not a new trend.

**After-hours earnings reactions**

- **APP +22.83% AH** — the headline after-hours event. Q3 revenue $2.185B (+55% y/y, +14% q/q, ~$100M above the high end of guidance), adj.
- EBITDA $1.84B (+59%, 84% margin), net income $1.44B (+72%), EPS $4.30 vs $3.94 Zacks consensus, FCF $1.4B (77% of adj.
- EBITDA), 4.1M shares repurchased for $1.4B with the authorization raised to $3.6B. Q4 guide $2.365–2.395B revenue (+43–44% y/y, +8–10% q/q) and $1.995–2.025B adj.
- EBITDA implies FY26 revenue and EBITDA growth >50%.
- **ADMA +28.24% AH** — EPS $0.22 (up 47% y/y) on revenue $141M (+5.1%); net income $50M. Stock had closed **−5.67%**, so the after-hours move is a full reversal.
- Priced move was ±15.06% — the print blew through it.
- **SEZL +26.93% AH** — revenue $167M (+42.6%), EPS $1.38 (+84%), net income $48M (+79.3%). Priced move was far smaller; a clear guidance-quality beat.
- **MNTN −39.73% AH / VCYT −30.06% AH / FSLY −16.28% AH / SNAP −11.46% AH** — Q3 reaction set.
- FSLY's drop is not purely earnings: the Go-To-Market leadership transition ran alongside the print.
- **Not sourced:** LYNX, RPD, LZ, BROS, HUBS, PLCE, AEHL — no catalyst I could verify. Listed without a reason rather than guessing.

**Open research queue**

- **Data-center policy is the live trade, not a one-day story.** HUT, STRL, CIFR, MOD and (indirectly) semis repriced on a *Texas pledge*, not on a federal rule.
- Track whether the pause becomes state legislation; if it does, the AI-infrastructure complex has a multi-quarter overhang that no intraday move prices.
- **Confirm the AstraZeneca–Rhythm deal.** RYTM +28% on a *reported* $10B offer.
- If a formal 8-K/merger agreement follows, biotech M&A re-rates broadly; if the report doesn't firm up, RYTM gives back the entire move. Highest-impact unverified item in this brief.
- **APP's gap vs its guidance.** A +22.8% after-hours move on a Q4 guide of +8–10% sequential revenue puts a lot of weight on Thursday's open.
- Watch whether analysts raise the FY26 numbers to match the implied >50% growth, and whether the name holds the pre-election low.
- **Thursday's 8:30 ET claims and Friday's payrolls.** VIX 16.61 is a bet that the macro cycle is not the next risk.
- The next two data points are the first chance to test it; a hot payroll print into a 16 VIX is the asymmetric case.
- **Energy's de-rating.** XLE −4.74% with crude only −1.2%, ahead of COP's print. If COP guides well and the sector still doesn't respond, the move is positioning, not fundamentals.
- **Gold and the dollar.** GLD +3.68%, gold futures +1.82%, DXY −0.30%, 10Y −5.8bp — all four consistent with a dovish-growth-shock read.
- Confirm whether this is the start of a gold bid or a one-session election hedge.
- **Verify the under-reported names.** LYNX, RPD, LZ, HUBS (after-hours) and ECG, LIME, SNDX, KURA, SUPN (regular session) had large moves with no verified catalyst in any source consulted —
- these are gaps, not clean narrative.
